Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning pro rata credits for service outages to telecommunications consumers.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the telecommunications consumer fairness act;adding a new chapter to Title 19 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The definitions in this section applythrough this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Person" means an individual, corporation, business trust,estate, trust, partnership, limited liability company, association,joint venture, government, governmental subdivision, agency orinstrumentality, public corporation, or any other legal or commercialentity. (2) "Service outage" means loss of a telecommunications serviceresulting from equipment failure not caused by the customer. (3) "Telecommunications service" means video, voice, music, or datadelivered for retail sale to the general public within the state bycoaxial cable, fiber optic cable, wireless transmission, or directbroadcast satellite.

Every person providing a telecommunicationsservice must provide pro rata credits to customers for service outages p. 1 SB 6197whenever that service is not available for a total of four hours ormore in a monthly billing cycle. The minimum amount of pro rata credita company must provide is the monthly cost of service divided bythirty, then multiplied by the number of days or portions of daysduring which service was not provided. This section does not preventa person from providing pro rata credits for service outages that totalless than four hours in a monthly billing cycle.

The legislature finds that the practicescovered by this chapter are matters vitally affecting the publicinterest for the purpose of applying the consumer protection act,chapter 19.86 RCW. A failure to provide a credit under this chapter isnot reasonable in relation to the development and preservation ofbusiness and is an unfair or deceptive act in trade or commerce and anunfair method of competition for the purpose of applying the consumerprotection act, chapter 19.86 RCW. In addition to any other penaltiesor remedies available under chapter 19.86 RCW, a person injured by aviolation of this chapter may bring an action for recovery ofliquidated damages in the amount of one thousand dollars per violation,plus court costs and attorneys' fees.
Sections 1 through 3 of this act constitutea new chapter in Title 19 RCW.
This act applies to contracts or franchiseagreements issued or renewed on or after the effective date of thissection.
